note: Volumes of the Russian Chthonic Atlas. 'published' volumes list plates through the `volume` field of data/plates.json; 'planned' entries are research leads, not content.

volumes.title: ARCHÆOLOGY OF RUSSIAN DEATH
volumes.subtitle: Threshold, body, ritual, table, grave, voice, afterlife, collective death, art, the Soviet afterlife, the archive
volumes.dek: The first volume: how people in Russia handled the dead, imagined what came after, and tried to keep a record of it.

volumes.title: THE CHTHONIC LANDSCAPE
volumes.subtitle: Houses, forests, waters, roads, villages and cellars as places where the living and the dead meet
volumes.dek: The second volume moves from the grave to the ground around it. Plates are published one at a time; the rest are listed with their scope and stay unpublished until their sources are checked.

volumes.title: THE UNSEEN
volumes.subtitle: Household spirits, the unquiet dead, the calendar of the dead, taboo and protection
volumes.dek: The third volume: household spirits, the unquiet dead, the calendar of the dead, taboo and protection. Each plate states its region, source and period, and none is offered as a unified pantheon.

volumes.title: MEMORY, CATASTROPHE AND MODERNITY
volumes.subtitle: Abandonment as material process; the digital afterlife
volumes.dek: Planned, with comparative dossiers on Old Believer, Muslim, Jewish, Buddhist and northern and Siberian Indigenous funerary traditions, each in its own context.

planned.title: The Materials of Abandonment
planned.scope: Ruined houses, neglected cemeteries, demolished churches, reused gravestones; physical decay tied to historical process.

planned.title: The Digital Afterlife
planned.scope: Online memorials, profiles of the dead, digital inheritance; treated as a serious contemporary extension, not a novelty.
